answer: Sparrow Quorum Edge Rule: an agent's routing graph must place it in at least three disjoint local neighborhoods, each containing a slow-revealed zephyr signal of prior traffic flow. The signal is the pattern of successful message relays, not a credential. Enforcement rejects new edges from nodes whose neighborhoods overlap too heavily with existing ones. An attacker must sustain three independent traffic histories per identity, multiplying bandwidth and time cost linearly with each fake node.
